title: fix(dedicated): stabilize burst controls and correct fleet utilization reporting regression
author: Ariana Chen
description: Fixes two related regressions in Dedicated fleet autoscaling: 1) a token-bucket replenishment race that could permanently starve burst capacity under heavy concurrent allocation, and 2) an aggregation bug in fleet utilization reporting that produced under-reported or negative utilization values in the daily summary. The change stabilizes the burst controller by serializing bucket updates with a lightweight compare-and-swap path and adding deterministic refunds on preempted allocations. Utilization reporting now uses a corrected time-window join and handles partial-shard gaps by backfilling with last-seen metrics to prevent skew. Also adds unit tests, integration tests, CI coverage for the new code paths, and observability improvements (prometheus metrics and dashboard notes). Includes a migration to backfill 7 days of summarized utilization where negative values were observed. Please see commits for details. Context: A production incident on 2026-02-08 exposed two issues: burst tokens not being returned when allocations were canceled mid-queue, and a downstream batch job aggregating shard-level throughput that incorrectly subtracted overlapping time windows leading to negative daily numbers. Both issues impacted Dedicated customers' perceived capacity and billing reconciliation. What I changed: serialized bucket updates in autoscaler/core/burst_bucket.go to ensure atomic replenish/refund semantics; added deterministic refund logic on allocation cancellation in autoscaler/manager/allocator.go; fixed fleet-level aggregation in observability/reports/utilization_aggregator.go by aligning join windows and adding backfill logic; added metrics autoscaler_burst_tokens_total and autoscaler_burst_token_errors_total; added e2e test suite test/dedicated/burst_replenish_e2e.test that reproduces the race and verifies token counts; added unit tests for aggregation edge cases; updated dashboards/docs in docs/dedicated/autoscaling.md to note the bug and the backfill migration. Testing: All unit tests and the new e2e tests were run in CI. Local stress runs (1000 concurrent allocation cycles over 30 minutes) showed stable token counts and no regressions in latency. Prometheus test harness validated the new metrics semantics. Rollout notes: This change is backward-compatible at the API level. The migration backfills up to 7 days of summarized utilization and runs as a low-priority background job; it will not impact live traffic. We plan a staged rollout: feature-flag disabled on main, enable for 10% of fleets for 24h, then full rollout. Related: Linear ENG-3124, ENG-3301.
